solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mr Right? Chancer and pig in Mr Wrong!

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so these letters are set out in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman lamenting that her supposed ideal man turned out to be an opportunist and a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong!' shuffles CHANCER, PIG, IN and MR together; 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale hero is the proverbial ideal suitor, the perfect partner a romantic hopes to meet.

clue.text: Structure for supporting managing director legal, there's power at the top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top comes first, so power leads

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: managing letters means handling and arranging them, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company's management chart: the legal director holds the power at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managing director' looks like a job title, but 'managing' rearranges DIRECTOR LEGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoulder girdle is the bony framework that supports the arms, a skeletal supporting structure.

clue.text: Lead-free metal is on gold tooth

indicators.note: free of its lead, its first letter, so the metal loses its opening letter

parts.note: zinc is a metal
taken as written
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gold tooth made of a lead-free metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead-free' reads as unleaded metal, but it means the metal loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A front cutting tooth is one of the types of tooth in the mouth, an example of the class.

clue.text: Fine form

definitions.meaning: first-rate, as in a ... act or a ... player
a school form, a group of pupils taught together

explanation.definitionFit: It means excellent informally, and also a year group of pupils, which Britons call a form.

clue.text: Gear stick, terribly hot when engaged

indicators.note: engaged as in held within, so the jumbled letters sit inside the word for stick

parts.note: to cling is to stick

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are in a bad state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver struggling with a gear stick that gets terribly hot when in gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear stick' reads as one car part, but 'Gear' is the definition and 'stick' is CLING; 'terribly' turns HOT into OTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothes, the things a person wears.

clue.text: An equal in conversation to come

indicators.note: words used in conversation are spoken, so we go by how they are heard

parts.note: a peer is an equal

explanation.surface: Someone joining a conversation on equal terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An equal' is A PEER, which when spoken matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up or show up is to come into view, so as a verb it is a synonym for arriving.

clue.text: I am at rest after breaking parts of the foot

indicators.note: breaking up the words lets the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient resting after breaking bones in the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' fits the injury story but rearranges I AM AT REST; 'after' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: These five long bones run between the ankle and the toes, so they are anatomical parts of the foot.

clue.text: Area for development certainly managed to turn around with right investment

indicators.note: investing here is clothing or enclosing, so the right letter goes inside
turned around means read backwards, so the two words reverse

parts.note: yes is a certain affirmative
to run something is to manage it; 'has run' is 'has managed'

explanation.surface: A property developer turning a site around with an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal gives NURSEY before the right letter goes in; 'investment' looks financial but means putting inside, as in investing a fort.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where young plants or children are raised and grow is an area where development happens.

clue.text: Intimate relation and drinkers entertained by South American statesman

indicators.note: hosted, held inside, so the statesman wraps the relation and drinkers

parts.note: Juan Perón was president of Argentina
a son is a relation
topers are heavy drinkers

explanation.surface: A relation and some drinkers being hosted by a South American leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained' sounds like hospitality but here means held inside; Perón was Argentina's president.
explanation.definitionFit: Direct, face-to-face and private, so something one-to-one between two people is intimate.

clue.text: Joyful band connected to woofer, by the sound of it

indicators.note: joined on to, so the band is attached directly after the dog
tells us the name of the dog is heard rather than spelt, giving a near-identical spoken form

parts.note: a woofer is a dog that barks; a cocker spaniel is one
a hoop is a band, as round a barrel

explanation.surface: A hi-fi enthusiast pleased with a band's sound through their new bass speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woofer' looks like a loudspeaker but is a barking dog, a cocker spaniel; said aloud COCKER gives COCKA.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cock-a-hoop is an idiom for being elated and triumphant, so it is a synonym of joyful.

clue.text: Short winter seemingly draws in

indicators.note: the words take in, or contain, the letters needed, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: An observation that winter days seem short as the evenings draw in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draws in' looks like the shortening of days but signals the answer is held within 'winter seemingly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A terse reply is brief and curt, so the word is a synonym of short in manner or length.

clue.text: Omani capital, a relative haven

indicators.note: a capital letter is the initial one, so we take the first letter of Omani

parts.note: a sister is a relative, shortened to sis

explanation.surface: A description of the Omani capital as relatively a safe haven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Muscat but means only the first letter of 'Omani'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in the desert is a refuge, so figuratively the word means a peaceful retreat or haven.

clue.text: Cold gas, natural

parts.note: helium is a gas, chemical symbol He
artless means natural, without guile or artifice

explanation.surface: A terse note about cold natural gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' looks like a temperature describing the gas but is the definition in the sense of unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cold in manner is unfeeling and without compassion, which is what lacking a heart means figuratively.

clue.text: Superior unqualified to cover leave, on reflection

indicators.note: the first word wraps around the second, covering it

parts.note: arrant means utter, unqualified, as in arrant nonsense

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, so the word for leave is read backwards

parts.note: to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone unqualified covering for a superior's leave, and thinking about it afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' reverses only GO, making OG, which ARRANT covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A superior air is haughty and conceited, so as an adjective it is a synonym of overbearing pride.

clue.text: Oil covering end of document on a large emblem of sovereignty

indicators.note: the oil covers, wraps around, the last letter

parts.note: grease is oil or lubricant

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: Oil daubed over the end of a document bearing a large royal emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts GREASE around T, the last letter of 'document'.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch's official seal on state documents signifies royal authority, an emblem of sovereignty.

clue.text: Item for colouring a source of light in blue

indicators.note: the light source sits inside the word for blue

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, abbreviated Con
a ray is a beam, a source of light

explanation.surface: A child's description of picking something to colour the sky blue with a ray of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' is not a colour here but a Tory: CON, the UK Conservative party, whose colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax or pencil stick used by children to add colour to pictures is a colouring item.

clue.text: Those burning wood among parts of a framework

indicators.note: placed in the middle of, so the wood sits within the bones

parts.note: bones are parts of the skeleton, the body's framework
fir is a type of wood

explanation.surface: Wood being burned among the remains of a framework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning wood' reads together, but 'Those burning' is the definition and 'wood' is FIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Large outdoor fires are things that burn, so they are those burning.

clue.text: Engine component to buy, with request for installation

indicators.note: the request is installed, put inside, the word for buy

parts.note: to get something is to buy or obtain it
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A mechanic buying a spare part and asking for it to be fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installation' fits the garage picture, but it only means one word is put inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal between engine parts, such as the head seal, is a component of an engine.

clue.text: Tongue rolling up berries, then I lick half off

indicators.note: in a down clue rolling up means reading upwards, so the berries are reversed

parts.note: haws are hawthorn berries

indicators.note: with half taken off only the first half of lick remains

explanation.surface: A tongue rolling up berries and licking half of them off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like the body part but means a language. 'rolling up' reverses HAWS to SWAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language, and this is the Bantu language widely spoken in East Africa.

clue.text: One jerk entering the game as a parliamentarian?

indicators.note: one jerk goes into the game, entering it

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
one is the Roman numeral I
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: An MP behaving like a jerk who has entered the game of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like an insult but is a twitch, TIC. The question mark flags a parliamentarian as one example of the wider class.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician, especially one keen on political manoeuvre; a member of parliament is one example.

clue.text: Begin, for example, as prime minister? Prime minister won't begin!

definitions.text: Begin, for example, as prime minister?

indicators.note: the name cannot begin, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister

explanation.surface: A puzzle about who Begin was as prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begin' is Menachem Begin, the Israeli prime minister, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Menachem Begin led Israel's government, so he is an example of a premier from that country.

clue.text: Flavour, one of four

definitions.meaning: to flavour food is to add salt and spices
spring, summer, autumn and winter are the four parts of the year

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means add taste with salt or spice; as a noun it is a quarter of the year.

clue.text: Grouse alongside pan, meat to cook

indicators.note: placed beside, so the complaint sits next to the criticism

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, to roast
to grouse is to complain, to beef

explanation.surface: A cook instructed to prepare a grouse alongside a pan of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' and 'pan' look like a game bird and a cooking vessel but are both verbs for complaining and criticising.
explanation.definitionFit: Ox meat cooked in the oven is the classic English Sunday joint, an example of meat.

clue.text: 'Swell' certainly describes 'good'

indicators.note: draws a line around, so the word for certainly encircles good

parts.note: sure means certainly, as in 'sure, I'll come'

explanation.surface: A comment on slang: 'swell' certainly means 'good'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' is used in its geometric sense of drawing around, so SURE goes around G.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell of the sea is a rise of water, so as a noun or verb it is a synonym of a sudden rush.

clue.text: Just over three entering water that's brown

indicators.note: going into, so the number goes inside the water

parts.note: sea is a body of water
pi is about 3.14, just over three

explanation.surface: Something just over three going into water and turning it brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just over three' is pi, roughly 3.14.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown tint, as in old photographs, made from cuttlefish ink; a shade of brown.

clue.text: Accumulated facts about current in European river

indicators.note: around, so the knowledge wraps the current symbol

parts.note: lore is accumulated knowledge or tradition
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A geography fact file on the current of a European river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' fits a river but is the physics symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest river in France, flowing west to the Atlantic, is an example of a European waterway.

clue.text: Consumed by anxiety, pal unfortunately lacking support

indicators.note: eaten up inside, so the jumbled friend goes within the worry

parts.note: stress is anxiety or strain

indicators.note: an unfortunate state is a muddled one, so the letters of pal are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend consumed by worry, unfortunately without anyone to support them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the friend into APL before the worry swallows it; 'support' hints at a dress without straps.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress or bra with no shoulder straps lacks that form of support, so the word describes being unsupported.

clue.text: Where Americans get their gas — the dentist's chair?

definitions.meaning: gas is American for petrol, bought at a garage forecourt
the place where teeth get their fillings, humorously named

explanation.surface: Musing on where Americans fill up, and where a patient gets gas at the dentist.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas also means the anaesthetic a dentist gives, which ties the two halves together.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage forecourt selling fuel is one sense; a place where cavities get stopped is the punning second.
